text: dsh-sandbox-console-fix 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端的 Windows 沙箱 bundle。它通过 Cordis patch 在 Windows 上替换 sandbox provider，并在 ACL runner 启动参数中预加载 console-shim.mjs，使 workspace-write 下的 pwsh、cmd 或 powershell 命令可启动。适合遇到该沙箱运行器兼容问题的 Windows 用户；需要 Harness bundle 环境，不要求 API key 或外部服务。

dsh-sandbox-console-fix is a Windows bundle for the DeepSeek Harness sandbox. It replaces the sandbox provider and preloads a shim in the ACL runner, helping workspace-write shell commands start. It requires Windows and Harness; no API key or external service is required.
Windows 桌面版 Harness 的 workspace-write shell 命令启动失败，怎么处理？
让 Windows 上的 DSH 沙箱能正常启动 pwsh 或 cmd 子进程。
How can I get sandboxed shell commands to start in the Windows desktop app?
该功能在 Windows 替换 sandbox provider，并预加载 shim，帮助 workspace-write 下的 shell 子进程启动。

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Prior art and corroboration：`@argszero/cordis-plugin-sandbox-grant-advisor` (0.17.0) already names this failure shape as its
`native-init` family and explains it: a confined child that never reaches its first instruction, split
into the packaged GUI-subsystem host and a console-subsystem `node.exe` whose runner was started with
`DETACHED_PROCESS`. It is an advisor — it names and diagnoses; this bundle is the repair. Its measured
remedies (Harness discussions #8193 / #8208) are followed here, including restoring the runner's three
standard handles around `AllocConsole()`. The longer mechanism write-up is discussion #9238, and the
report is #9280.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Root cause and what this bundle does：The restricted token that runs the confined child gets **one** extra full-access ACE merged into its
Default DACL: `tempWriteSidPtr ?? writeSidPtr ?? worldSid` — the capability write SID in
`workspace-write`, `Everyone` in `read-only`. On a host whose process token's Default DACL lacks
`Everyone`, a child that has to create a console during DLL initialization dies with `0xC0000142` — and
it only has to when the sandbox runner owns no console (the packaged desktop app's Electron host).

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Root cause and what this bundle does：**Primary mechanism (since 0.2.0).** The shim runs inside the runner process *before* the runner derives
the restricted token, and merges `Everyone` into that process token's Default DACL. The restricted token
inherits it, which is exactly what the shipped `read-only` path already does — so no console handling is
needed at all.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Root cause and what this bundle does：**Fallback.** If the merge cannot be applied, the shim gives the runner a console instead:
`AllocConsole()` with the three standard handles saved and restored and the window hidden.

text:
dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The problem：On the packaged Windows desktop app, any shell call under **`workspace-write`** fails immediately:

```
[exit code: 3221225794]        # 0xC0000142 STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED
```

`pwsh`, `cmd` and `powershell` all fail the same way, both MSI and Store-packaged PowerShell builds,
while `danger-full-access` **and `read-only`** work — so the shell tool is fine and the
**`workspace-write` confinement path** is the problem.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The problem：The failure needs two conditions together — a **console-less runner host** (the Electron binary) and
`workspace-write`. The complete matrix is in [`docs/VERIFICATION.md`](docs/VERIFICATION.md#3-the-failure-matrix). Why the child's own console creation succeeds in the one mode and fails in the other is **not isolated** — see sections 5 and 9 of that record; the fix works in both modes either way.

Root cause, in the shipped code (`dsh-sandbox-local`, `windowsAclRunnerInvocation()`):

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The problem：```js
if (existsSync(builtEntry)) return [process.execPath, builtEntry];
```

In the desktop app `process.execPath` is **`DeepSeek Harness.exe`** — an **Electron binary, i.e. a
GUI-subsystem image, which never has a console**. Measured on one machine, same parent process:

| runner host | `GetConsoleWindow()` |
|---|---|
| `node.exe` (console subsystem) | non-zero → has a console |
| `DeepSeek Harness.exe` (GUI subsystem) | `0` → no console |

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The problem：The ACL runner then spawns the confined child **without** `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`
— on purpose, because per DSH's own documentation such children die during DLL initialization under
the restricted token — and relies on the child **inheriting the runner's console**. With nothing to
inherit, the console-subsystem child must create a console itself; that creation fails under the
Low-integrity write-restricted token, and the process exits `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED` (`0xC0000142`).

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The fix：One extra argv entry, in the position DSH's **own development path** already uses for the same runner
(`[process.execPath, "--import", <url>, entry]`):

```
shipped:  [execPath, runner.js, …profile, --, target]
this:     [execPath, --import <console-shim.mjs>, runner.js, …profile, --, target]
```

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · The fix：`console-shim.mjs` merges one `Everyone` full-access ACE into the runner process token's Default DACL (falling back to `AllocConsole()` only when that cannot be applied), so the
confined child inherits a console and starts normally.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · What does **not** change：| | shipped | with this bundle |
|---|---|---|
| restricted token (Low IL + write-restricted SIDs) | ✔ | **identical** — except the token's *Default DACL* gains an `Everyone` full-access ACE, exactly the ACE the shipped `read-only` path already merges |
| workspace / private-temp capability-SID grants, deny ACEs | ✔ | **identical** |
| integrity label, Job object, stdio plumbing, denial dialects | ✔ | **identical** |
| runner and child environment | ✔ | **identical — nothing injected** |
| `dsh-fs-sandbox` file policy | ✔ | **untouched** |

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · What does **not** change：Verified with an escape-write test run *inside* the confined child: four out-of-workspace targets are
denied and absent on disk, while an in-workspace write succeeds — see
[`docs/VERIFICATION.md`](docs/VERIFICATION.md).

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Install：Install it the way dsh expects — through the **Plugin Manager**, which performs package installation
and bundle selection itself:

1. Open the Plugin Manager page and install a bundle from
   `https://github.com/TJZF-4j97/dsh-sandbox-console-fix`, or from an absolute path to a checkout of
   this directory.
2. Restart the Harness.
3. Set the session to `workspace-write` and run any shell command.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Install：Nothing is downloaded and no build script is requested, because the package deliberately declares no
dependencies: `index.js` loads `LocalSandboxProvider` from the running Harness bundle, and
`console-shim.mjs` resolves `koffi` there too. The Harness's own installer recorded exactly that —
`Packages: +1`, zero downloads, no pending build scripts.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Install：`cordis.patch.yml` mounts this provider by **disabling the shipped `sandbox` row and inserting its own**,
both rows platform-guarded with `!!js` — the idiom the shipped `dsh-base` patch uses for its own
`bash-sandbox` row. That shape is required by the Loader dialect: a non-insert patch that targets an
existing row replaces its fields, and a truthy `name` only *asserts* the existing plugin name, so a
provider row cannot be swapped by overriding its id. On Windows the composition keeps exactly one
`ctx.sandbox` provider and the shipped package still resolves from the dsh installation; on other
platforms the shipped row stays enabled and this bundle's row stays disabled.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Install：<details>

Copy the directory somewhere the profile can resolve, add the name to `dsh.profile.bundles`, then
restart:

```powershell
Copy-Item -Recurse -Force .\dsh-sandbox-console-fix "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-sandbox-console-fix"
```

```json
{ "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-sandbox-console-fix"] } } }
```

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Install：The Plugin Manager route is preferred: `install_bundle` snapshots and restores `package.json` and
`pnpm-lock.yaml` when an install fails, and keeps the profile's own bookkeeping consistent.
</details>

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Verify：> **Not caused by this bundle:** inside the confined shell the sandbox blocks piped stdio between
> programs, so `$x = & some.exe …` and `some.exe | Out-Null` fail (`EPERM`; PowerShell surfaces it as
> `StandardOutputEncoding is only supported when standard output is redirected`), while a bare
> `& some.exe …`, PowerShell's own cmdlet pipelines and file redirection work. That is the sandbox's
> documented confinement.
Reproduce the underlying mechanism without installing anything:

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Verify：```powershell
node scripts/console-probe.cjs                        # host-console probe
node scripts/console-probe.cjs --host electron        # same parent, Electron host
node scripts/full-chain-repro.js --help               # drive the shipped runner under both hosts
powershell -File scripts/escape-test.ps1 -Workspace <dir>   # confinement check

See [`scripts/README.md`](scripts/README.md) for the extracted-runner paths those scripts need.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Uninstall：Remove the bundle name from the profile's `bundles` list (and the dependency), then restart. No
system-level change is left behind — the workspace ACEs and integrity label that the Harness itself
owns are not touched by this bundle.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Compatibility：Because it subclasses a Harness-internal class, re-check after a Harness upgrade — the upstream fix
(see the issue report) makes this package unnecessary.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Discovery：DeepSeek Harness's [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
asks ecosystem plugins to associate their GitHub project with the **`dsh-plugin`** topic. This
repository carries it — together with `dsh`, `deepseek-harness`, `sandbox`, `windows` and `pwsh` — so
the plugin is discoverable from that topic listing.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · Security：The bundle does not widen file authority, and this is measured rather than argued: with the Default-DACL
merge applied, writes to `%USERPROFILE%`, the drive root, `C:\Windows\Temp` and the user temp directory
are still denied and the files are absent, while an in-workspace write succeeds. What changes is only the
runner process token's **Default DACL**, which gains one `Everyone` full-access ACE — the same ACE the
shipped runner already merges on its `read-only` path. The restricting SIDs, the Low integrity label, the
workspace and private-temp grants, the denial ACEs and the fs policy are untouched, and the shim performs
no process creation and no environment change. It writes one file only when
`DSH_SANDBOX_CONSOLE_FIX_DEBUG` is explicitly set to a path, for support. Every failure is swallowed so
the runner keeps its shipped behaviour.

dsh-sandbox-console-fix README · What this bundle changes, precisely：* It merges one `Everyone` full-access ACE into the **runner process token's Default DACL**, before the
  runner derives the restricted token — the same ACE the shipped runner already merges on its
  `read-only` path. The restricted token therefore inherits it.
* Scope: a Default DACL governs the initial ACL of **every securable object** that token holder creates
  without an explicit security descriptor, so this is process-wide for the runner, not limited to the
  confined child. It is per-process and disappears when the Harness exits.
* Measured after the fix: the confined child starts, its own restricted token's Default DACL contains
  the `Everyone` ACE with mask `0x1f01ff`, writes outside the workspace stay denied and absent, and the
  child's own console is created hidden.
* **Uninstall this bundle before validating a Harness upgrade** — while it is installed, its `disabled`
  patch silently discards any upstream change to the shipped `sandbox` row.
